title: Prefill Probe: Kernel Swarm Benchmark and CI Canary
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, portable benchmark harness and CI canary specifically targeting prefill+decode scheduling and kernel selection interplay across representative attention patterns. This ticket delivers: (1) a kernel-swarm microbenchmark that runs small randomized prefill traces on each kernel routing configuration; (2) a stochastic prefilling probe that injects real trace replays and synthetic attention shapes (long-context, strided attention, short queries with wide KV reuse); (3) CI perf gate definitions and sentinel thresholds suitable for PR-level and nightly runs; and (4) a compact telemetry contract (metrics/tags) so Console dashboards and perf alerts can pick up regressions without high noise.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Kickoff: scoped microbench and probe shapes; decided to focus first on Llama3-like families and one decoder-only GPT variant for coverage.

2025-02-22 - Design review: agreed to use deterministic RNG seeds for synthetic generators and keep trace replays truncated to 10k tokens per run to bound CI time. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Prefill+Probe+Design
2025-02-25 - Infra: test runners provisioned on ephemeral GPU pool (ci-tag: prefprobe); small helper container: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime-prefprobe:latest
2025-03-01 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567 - adds kernel-swarm harness and synthetic generators. Needs benchmark owner review.

2025-03-02 - Observability: telemetry schema proposed in PR 4567; awaiting telemetry-owner signoff. Noted potential tag cardinality with model_family+kernel_id; recommendation to limit model_family to coarse families.
